name: Posts
summary: Drafts of what this project will say outside itself, the accounts it says them as, and the text of everything already said.
description: Posts holds three things. A channel is one account this project publishes as — which network, whose account, where inside it the posts go where the network needs telling, and a credential kept in this machine's vault under a name the record carries, never in the record itself. A draft is what the project is about to say, written for one channel, with the room left in it counted down as somebody writes. A publication is what it said, carrying the text exactly as it went out and the identifier the network issued, so editing a draft afterwards cannot rewrite the account of it. All three are ordinary records: they live in the project's memory, travel with the repository, and can be written or read by an agent as easily as by a person — while the credential stays on the machine and travels nowhere. Publishing is a person's act: they read the exact text and press the button, there is no clock in here, and nothing sends anything while nobody is looking. Four networks are reached from this window — LinkedIn, Bluesky, Threads and Telegram — and a Telegram channel says what it is: a bot posting into a chat, not a person speaking.

areas.label: Posts
areas.description: Drafts waiting to be said, the accounts they go out as, and what has already gone.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Publish one draft to the channel it names, and answer with what the network called the post. Sync makes the request; you never see the credential and cannot choose the account. Afterwards write a posts.publication from the answer and archive the draft — nothing else records it.

draft.description: The key of the posts.draft record to publish. It must already name a channel that somebody has connected.
